newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe dollar falls, central bank stands aloof.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe dollar falls, central bank stands aloof.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar, which shed one percent against the U.S. currency last week on the back of import pressure, extended the loss to 1.3 percent on Tuesday as hopes of central bank support waned, dealers said.

Dealers were optimistic on Monday that the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe would pump money into the system to shore up the Zimbabwe dollar after a meeting on Friday revealed that the market was more short of foreign currency than previously thought.
But on Tuesday the central bank was still showing reluctance to step in, causing worry within the market that the Zimbabwe dollar might go into free-fall.
"The market is still short and it doesn't seem like the central bank is interested in coming in to support the local dollar," one foreign exchange dealer said.
"Maybe they are happy to see the local currency fall, but I think it has been too sudden....they should have come in to smoothe the fall," he added.

Another said while last week's wave of importer demand had thinned out somewhat, the market was still cautious and most players were holding on to their foreign currency reserves for their own customers, quoting high offer prices to scare off potential buyers.
"People are now reluctant to sell and have hiked their offer prices by two points to protect their positions," one said.

Market analysts have predicted a further depreciation of the Zimbabwe dollar in coming months, particularly in October as tobacco sales, currently bringing in a steady inflow of export receipts, draw to an close.

Some say a fall in the local currency would be good for the country's economy. They argue that the Zimbabwe dollar is over-valued and is disadvantaging exporters, especially to South Africa, Zimbabwe's major trading partner in Africa.

At Tuesday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 10.1200/1500 against the U.S. dollar, down from Monday's 10.0900/1200, while against sterling it slipped to 15.7630/8180 from 15.7050/7610. It was at 6.8540/8770 from 6.8280/8500 versus the mark and fell to 2.2350/2440 from 2.2220/2310 against South Africa's rand.
